items.text: Had we known about the delay earlier, we could have warned our key customers in time.
The figures would appear to suggest that demand is levelling off rather than falling.
What concerns me most is not the cost itself but the lack of transparency around it.
Not only did the launch go smoothly, but it also exceeded our most optimistic forecasts.
We are under no obligation to accept the revised terms, but it might be wise to do so.
The distributor has agreed in principle, subject to a few minor changes in the contract.
It remains to be seen whether the new pricing strategy will pay off in the long run.
Given the circumstances, I think we handled a very awkward situation remarkably well.
The proposal was turned down on the grounds that it would stretch our budget too far.
Rarely have I seen a team pull together so effectively under such intense pressure.
Should you have any further questions, please do not hesitate to get in touch with me.
The merger is widely believed to have been driven by tax considerations rather than strategy.
Let's not lose sight of the fact that our core customers value reliability above price.
By the time the report reaches the board, most of the key decisions will have been made.
There is mounting evidence that the campaign has failed to strike a chord with younger buyers.
Much as I sympathise with their position, I cannot see how we could justify the expense.
Profits fell short of expectations, largely owing to a sharp rise in energy costs.
The new regulations come into force in January, so we need to act without delay.
It was only when we compared the two sets of data that the discrepancy became apparent.
On balance, the benefits of relocating the warehouse would seem to outweigh the drawbacks.

items.speak: Well, the new system is certainly faster, I'll give them that. But nobody asked the people who actually use it every day, and frankly, it shows. Half the features we relied on have simply vanished.
items.prompt: What is the speaker's attitude to the new system?
options: anger at how fast things changed
items.explanation: 'I'll give them that' concedes a point, then 'But…' criticises.

items.speak: I was fully prepared to hate the conference, to be honest. Three days of presentations isn't my idea of fun. But I came away with two solid leads and, more surprisingly, a few genuinely new ideas.
items.prompt: How does the speaker feel about the conference now?
items.explanation: Low expectations, then 'more surprisingly, a few genuinely new ideas'.

items.speak: Look, I'm not saying the forecast is wrong. I'm just saying it rests on some fairly heroic assumptions about the exchange rate, and I'd rather we didn't bet the whole budget on it.
options: expressing cautious doubt about a forecast
items.answer: expressing cautious doubt about a forecast
items.explanation: 'Heroic assumptions' = unrealistically optimistic; the speaker hedges ('I'm not saying… I'm just saying').

items.speak: Oh, marvellous. Another reorganisation. That's the third one in two years, and I'm sure this one will fix everything, just like the last two did.
items.explanation: 'Marvellous' and 'just like the last two did' mean the opposite of what they say.

items.speak: I completely understand why the client is upset, and I'd probably feel the same in their position. That said, we did warn them about the risks in writing. Twice.
items.prompt: What is the speaker's main purpose?
options: to show sympathy while defending the company
to end the relationship with the client
items.answer: to show sympathy while defending the company
items.explanation: Empathy first, then 'That said…' introduces the defence.

items.speak: To be fair to the marketing team, the budget was cut halfway through the campaign. You can't really expect miracles with half the money, can you?
items.explanation: 'To be fair to…' signals a defence.

items.speak: Honestly? I think we're overthinking this. The client wants a simple answer, and we keep sending them forty-page reports. Let's just pick up the phone.
options: taking a simpler, more direct approach
waiting for the client to call
items.answer: taking a simpler, more direct approach

items.speak: It's not that I object to working from home as such. What bothers me is that the decisions now seem to happen in private chats that half the team never sees.
items.prompt: What is the speaker's main concern?
options: a lack of transparency in decision-making
items.answer: a lack of transparency in decision-making
items.explanation: 'It's not that… What bothers me is…' — the cleft points to the real issue.
